cases.name: Unit Tests
cases.description: Tests in test_unit.py — every function on a small hand-made example you can check by hand (three members, six orders, three square ZIP codes): the spatial join (add_zips, zip_centers), the features (add_features), your classifier's contract and six textbook visits, the tables (busy_table, reason_table, monthly_sales, members_by_zip, add_anchor_zip, demand_by_zip) and the site score; and each chart builder, by looking inside what it returns (heatmap cells, violins, Plotly traces, Folium markers and lines, choropleth values).

levels.label: More than 1/2 of the unit tests pass
Half or fewer of the unit tests pass

cases.name: Pipeline & App Tests
cases.description: Tests in test_pipeline.py — the whole year of data: every member placed in a ZIP, a visit per order, your classifier scored by the CENT portal against the survey (at least 85% agreement overall and 60% for every reason), the tables on all orders, the decision (shop #4 goes to 13057), and the dashboard driven with AppTest (title, four tabs, the shop and member pickers, the metrics, the maps and the winner).

levels.label: All pipeline and app tests pass
More than 1/2 of the pipeline and app tests pass
At least one pipeline or app test passes
No pipeline or app tests pass

cases.name: Code Structure Tests
cases.description: Tests in test_code.py — the source is parsed and checked for how it is built: the ZIPs come from a GeoPandas spatial join and centers from a projected centroid; the features merge and use haversine_km on whole columns; the classifier uses both time and distance; the tables use pivot_table, groupby and merge, not loops; each chart uses its lesson's library (seaborn heatmap and violinplot, Plotly line and choropleth_map, Folium Map, Marker, CircleMarker and PolyLine); the dashboard assembles the package.

levels.label: More than 1/2 of the code structure tests pass
Half or fewer of the code structure tests pass

cases.name: Code style & readability
cases.description: Code is for computers AND humans. Four checks on everything in code/, the same ones `ruff check` and a read of your code will show you before you submit (README Reference #14). All four must pass for the point.

requirements.name: No TODO comments left
requirements.description: Every # TODO from the starter code is done and deleted.

requirements.name: No leftover pass stubs
requirements.description: Every function the starter left as `pass` is implemented.

requirements.name: Every function has a docstring
requirements.description: Each function says what it does in a docstring.

requirements.name: No lint errors
requirements.description: `ruff check` reports nothing (pycodestyle + pyflakes rules, line length 88).

cases.name: Reflection
cases.description: Now that you've completed the assignment, think about what you did and share your thoughts. What did you learn? What confuses you? Where did you struggle? Where might you need more practice? A good reflection is **as specific as possible**, **uses the terminology of the problem domain** (what was learned in class / through readings), and **is actionable** (you can pursue next steps, or be aided in the pursuit).

levels.label: Excellent
levels.description: Well written, clear, and actionable. Uses terminology of the problem domain. Specific about what was learned and where more practice is needed.

levels.label: Needs Improvement
levels.description: Missing one of: well written, actionable, clear, uses terminilogy specific to assignment, demonstrated what was learned.
